FeedForward & Representation Learning

Word Embeddings: suppose e:V→R1×de: V → R^{1×d} e:V→R1×d﻿ is a function. A word w∈Vw ∈ Vw∈V﻿ is said to have a word embedding x∈R1×dx ∈ R^{1×d}x∈R1×d﻿ if x=e(w)x = e(w)x=e(w)﻿

  • important since NN cannot deal with text
  • this is an alternative wrt one-hot encoding
  • the embedding functions will never be written in closed form, but they will be always learned from the data

The simplest form of embedding function is to store directly the embeddings inside a matrix

An embedding layer with dimension ddd﻿ is a linear layer whose inputs are one-hot embeddings. Its weight matrix E∈R∣V∣×dE ∈ R^{|V|×d}E∈R∣V∣×d﻿ is called embedding matrix.

  • eie_iei​﻿ is a latent representation of a word in the latet space (vector space)
  • A non-linear function σ:R→Rσ : R → Rσ:R→R﻿ is called activation function

Feed-Forward Layer: suppose σσσ﻿ is an activation function and y=xWy = xWy=xW﻿ is a linear layer with nnn﻿ inputs, mmm﻿ outputs, and weight matrix W∈Rn×mW ∈ R^{n×m}W∈Rn×m﻿

  • A feed-forward layer is a parametrised function whose output y∈R1×my ∈ R^{1×m} y∈R1×m﻿ for the input x∈R1×nx ∈ R^{1×n}x∈R1×n﻿ is computed as y=σ(xW)y = σ(xW)y=σ(xW)﻿

Representation Learning

Learning word embeddings is interesting also per se

  • The cosine similarity between two different words encoded by one-hot encodings is always zero → thus totally unrelated
  • it makes sense to decouple the learning of the word embeddings from the learning of the language model → word2vec models at google

Continous Bag of Words Model (CBOW)

This model relies on the idea that “a word’s meaning is given by the words that frequently appear close-by”, known as distributional hypothesis, and then it learns the word embedding of a word in a sequence leveraging both the preceding and the following words

  • A 2m2m2m﻿ context windows is given by mmm﻿ preceding words and mmm﻿ successive words → f(wc)=P[wc∣wc−m...wc+w]f(w_c) = P[w_c | w_{c-m}...w_{c+w}]f(wc​)=P[wc​∣wc−m​...wc+w​]﻿

Our goal is to learn the word embedding ec∈R1×de_c ∈ R^{1×d}ec​∈R1×d﻿ of the center word wcw_cwc​﻿ for all words in TTT﻿

  • we use an embedding layer with weight matrix E∈R∣V∣×dE ∈ R^{|V|×d}E∈R∣V∣×d﻿, that will contain the word embeddings for all our words
    • ei=xiEe_i = x_i Eei​=xi​E﻿

The simplest way to compute the embedding of the central word is to average the context embeddings:

Now we convert the word embedding ece_cec​﻿ back to a probability distribution using a linear layer with weight matrix U∈Rd×∣V∣U ∈ R^{d×|V|}U∈Rd×∣V∣﻿ followed by a softmax function

  • f(wc)=P[wc∣wc−m...wc+w]=softmax(y)=softmax(ecU)f(w_c) = P[w_c | w_{c-m}...w_{c+w}] = \text{softmax}(y) = \text{softmax}(e_c U)f(wc​)=P[wc​∣wc−m​...wc+w​]=softmax(y)=softmax(ec​U)﻿

Skipgram Model

We want to learn P[wc−m...wc+w∣wc]P[ w_{c-m}...w_{c+w} | w_c]P[wc−m​...wc+w​∣wc​]﻿

The embeddings of common words is a lot more precise since is encountered a lot of times

  • What happens when a word has two meanings? It is the average of all the meanings → this words embeddings are called static word embeddings
